name: Burkina Faso
summary_text: Burkina Faso is dangerous for trans visitors. In July 2024 the military junta approved a revised Personal and Family Code criminalising homosexuality — Burkina Faso had never previously outlawed it. The junta (Traoré) has clamped down on opposition and media, promised elections have not been held, and much of the country faces jihadist insurgency. Enforcement details of the new law remain unclear (HDT notes drafting uncertainty), but the direction and the absence of any institutional recourse are unambiguous. For a visitor: new criminalisation under a junta, plus severe general security conditions.

sources.title: Burkina Faso's military junta to ban homosexual acts
sources.claim_summary: BBC (July 2024): Burkina Faso's military junta approved legislation to ban homosexual acts - previously not outlawed though socially frowned upon. Justice Minister Edasso Rodrigue Bayala announced the cabinet approval as part of a marriage-law overhaul that recognises only religious and customary marriages; the law still needed passage by the military-controlled parliament and junta leader Traoré's signature.

sources.title: Severe penalties for homosexuality in Burkina Faso | Africanews
sources.claim_summary: Africanews (July 2024): the junta approved revised marriage-family legislation criminalising homosexuality with 'severe penalties', as part of the same overhaul recognising only religious and customary marriages. (Article body largely behind page furniture at fetch time.)

US State Department 2011 Human Rights Report for Burkina Faso: pre-criminalisation baseline - no law criminalising same-sex conduct; documents security-force abuses, prison conditions and societal discrimination (no LGBT-specific section content in the retrieved text).

sources.title: Burkina Faso Criminalizes Same-Sex Conduct | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW (Sept 2025): Burkina Faso criminalises same-sex conduct - the junta's law took effect, with prison sentences; HRW's reporting on the new penal provisions.

sources.title: Burkina Faso parliament passes law outlawing LGBTQ practices | CNN
sources.claim_summary: CNN (Sep 2025): 'Burkina Faso parliament passes law outlawing LGBTQ practices' — a new criminal-code article punishes 'LGBTQ practices' with up to five years.

sources.title: Nation of Burkina Faso will start throwing gay people in jail - LGBTQ Nation
sources.claim_summary: LGBTQ Nation (Sept 2025): Burkina Faso's junta unanimously passed a law banning homosexuality - 2-5 years' imprisonment plus fines, per Justice Minister Edasso Rodrigue Bayala; foreigners will be deported under the law; the country had never previously banned homosexuality.
